answer: A fresh identity starts with zero reputation, so a fake swarm must fund many bonds and survive a long voyage of audits before earning any nectar of influence. Sybil resistance here uses a staked-identity ledger: each agent must lock a bond before voting, and peers sample its work history through a prism of independent attestations. Attackers thus pay real capital plus audit time per identity, while legitimate agents amortize one bond across many epochs, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0057's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
